mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) over a 3-month period indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances when RSAFS shows a 3-month sustained increase.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals economic weakness, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over a 3-month period indicates supply-side constraints, which can lead to inflationary pressures and reduced corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) coupled with a decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a 3-month period signals a robust economic expansion, boosting consumer confidence and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases & UNRATE decreases over 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 45% of the instances when both trigger conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over a 3-month period, coupled with a stable or decreasing unemployment rate (UNRATE), indicates a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases & UNRATE stable/decreases over 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when both trigger conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over a 3-month period, coupled with a stable or decreasing federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS), suggests inflationary pressures without corresponding monetary tightening, which can lead to higher equity valuations due to increased nominal earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases & FEDFUNDS stable/decreases over 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of the instances when both trigger conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% in a quarter signals a contraction in economic activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.
